slides.h: Dining tables: splurge on //solid wood//, skip the seats for eight.
slides.dek: The hardest-working surface in the house is the wrong place to save.

slides.h: A table bought for two dinners a year.
body: The eight-seater fills the room so the big night looks right. The other 363 days it is a corridor squeeze and a dust field.
Buy for the daily four. Extend, borrow, or move the party when the crowd comes.
Hot pans, homework, a decade of elbows. A solid top takes all of it and sands back to new. Veneer gets one chip, and the chip is forever.
Counted per year of service, the solid table is the cheapest thing in the room.
Seats live under the table edge and under people. Sturdy and comfortable is the whole job.
Put the difference into the top, and upgrade seats one at a time as better ones turn up.

slides.h: Knock on the top before you pay.
body: Solid wood answers with a dense knock; veneer over board sounds hollow and light. The edge tells the same story: real grain wraps over it.
Ten seconds at the showroom saves the regret at home.

slides.h: Save this before the table hunt.
